- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, model tends to underreact — adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days — reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.5) and forecast is below recent trend, model underestimates bullish momentum — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment.
- Model consistently underpredicts true price in early days of a 30-day horizon — add 0.5–1.5% to first 3–5 forecasted days to account for lag.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.2–0.5) and price is trending sideways, model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, model is lagging — apply a 1–2% upward correction to next forecast horizon.
